Hector (PM): Quick thread to capture the 'escape lane' idea for Dedicated pools — customers want predictable short bursts without being dropped to best-effort. Proposal: configure per-contract "escape lanes" that reserve a tiny transient headroom and convert incoming requests to queued tokens with guaranteed dequeue rate. Thoughts?

Tom (Eng): I like it. Need to decide if escape lane is a separate logical queue or an annotation on existing queue slots. Separate queue simplifies accounting.

Rina (SRE): Operational concerns: reserve increases overall pressure. We should only allow escape lanes up to a percent of pool (suggest 3-7%). Also require a hard global cap to avoid noisy neighbor windows.

Nina (Sales): From customers: they care more about predictability than absolute capacity. They prefer a contract option like "burst window: X req/min for Y minutes" and a dashboard meter.

Hector (PM): Proposed contract knobs: burst_window_minutes, burst_rate_rps, max_burst_boost_pct. Mapping to implementation: burst credits consumed per request = tokens_per_request, recharge interval = 1s.

Tom (Eng): Implementation sketch:
```yaml
escape_lane:
  enabled: true
  burst_window_minutes: 15
  burst_rate_rps: 4.0
  max_burst_boost_pct: 5
  token_model: "tokens_per_request"
```
Queue behavior: if tenant has credits -> route to escape_lane queue which has priority boost but bounded dequeue. When credits exhausted, fall back to normal backfill behavior.

Rina (SRE): Add safety: if pool throttle > 4% or infra alerts fire, auto-suspend all escape lanes and emit events. Also log last_escape_use per tenant for billing and debugging.

CapacityBot: Note: metric created -> dedicated.escape_lane_usage_seconds. Alert threshold suggested at 95th percentile > 0 for >= 10m.

Hector (PM): Launch criteria draft: (1) correct credit accounting (unit tests + sim), (2) canary with 2 customers, (3) Console shows live burst credits and projected depletion, (4) SLO check: p99 latency delta for non-burst tenants < 3%.

Tom (Eng): Edge case: stateful sessions with KV cache. If escape lane routes a request but the session isn't hot, we may incur cold-starts. Suggest prefer warm sessions for escape lane or charge extra tokens.

Nina (Sales): Also need clear billing language. Customers expect simple overage: either included bursts per month or pay-per-burst-credit. I'll draft two billing models for legal.

Rina (SRE): Runbook items: how to disable per-tenant, emergency suspend for pool, telemetry fields to add: escape_lane_used, credits_remaining, suspend_reason.

Hector (PM): Owners: Tom + Rina to produce design and sim harness; Nina to draft customer pricing; I'll assemble launch checklist + docs. Aim: prototype in next sprint.

Tom (Eng): Ack. Will start a lightweight sim and PR for config schema.

Rina (SRE): Ack. Will add alert and runbook placeholders.

Nina (Sales): Ack. Will reach out to two pilot customers.

Hector (PM): Great. Keeping this thread for updates; will post doc link and simulation results here. :white_check_mark:
